title.narrative: Providing Life-Saving Assistance to Populations Affected by cyclical shocks induced by climate in Burundi

description.narrative: During the 2023-2024 rainy season, nearly 300,000 people were affected by El Nino and 102,000 were internally displaced. Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI), WASH and food are the most urgent needs according to the latest MSLA conducted in May 2024. Gaps in resource mobilization in Burundi have widened from 54% in 2021 to 71% in 2024 - with crucial sectors such as Shelter & Non-Food Items and Water, Hygiene and Sanitation severely underfunded. Nearly 90,000 internally displaced people in Burundi today, over 90% of whom are displaced by cyclical climate-induced shocks. More than 80,440 people have benefited from emergency shelter and essential goods assistance from the UN, international NGOs and local NGO partners in the sectors. This represents 60% of the population targeted by the shelter sector in the Inter-agency Flash Appeal published in 2024 for the El Nino response. As a response, UNHCR intends to provide a Shelter response targeting near 2,555 individuals, through (1) shelter construction for IDPs. The following activities are planned:The Gateri site, located in the Commune of Buganda within Cibitoke Province, is being developed to better accommodate internally displaced persons (IDPs) who are currently housed at the Mubimbi site. Despite requiring some refurbishment and the addition of trees and communal spaces, Gateri offers a more secure and dignified living environment than Mubimbi. The latter was found unsuitable due to its vulnerability to strong winds, prompting a relocation initiative by the Burundian government. At Gateri, 511 transitional shelters are being constructed, each at a cost of $2487 and equipped with a family latrine. These latrines, known as AKASUGA eco-latrine systems, are well-regarded across various provinces for their sustainability; the sludge from these units can be repurposed as compost or agricultural fertilizer, enhancing both sanitation and environmental stewardship. The displaced population is comprised mostly of women and children. Focus group discussions revealed that following the flooding, most of the men left their households and went in search for livelihoods elsewhere. This has left the female and child-headed households more vulnerable to protection risks, such as, GBV and other forms of exploitation, including trafficking. Other vulnerable groups in the IDP population are persons living with disability and the elderly who, due to their fragility, may face challenges in exercising income generating activities. The IDPs also face challenges with social integration in their new locations and access to basic services. There may not be adequate opportunities for the IDPs to participate in the decision-making processes concerning them. Youth have been left idle which has resulted in juvenile delinquency. This project will thus endeavor to include the affected population throughout the programming cycle, and to give special consideration to the vulnerable population. To the extent possible, the affected population will be engaged in the construction activities on a cash for work basis. Shelters constructed will be adapted to the needs of persons with disability.
